post.description: Run a backtest on the model's stored NAVs and keep it; ``save`` keeps it for good.
Try every split of the model's funds and rank them; nothing is stored.

patch.description: Save a run (with an optional name), or unsave it.

get.description: This run less an earlier one: final value, ratios and the weights that changed.
Return, drawdown and money in and out for a window of a run.
Real buckets first, then paper ones, with what each holds.

delete.description:
Delete a bucket. A paper bucket's purchases and SIPs go with it; a real bucket's stay,
in no bucket.

put.description: Rename it or change its model. Paper or real changes only while it's empty.

get.description: My cash accounts, totals per earmark, and the emergency money against its goal.
Compare buckets on their time-weighted growth, with what the money in each made.

Compare funds over the dates they all have, or from ``start`` for the funds that go
back that far, against ``benchmark_id`` or the default benchmark.

Compare models as if each were one fund: a lump sum split by its weights and
rebalanced as it says.

post.description: Return the payload unchanged, so tests can prove amounts and timestamps survive.

get.description: Where the phone sends its lots, and what the last import brought in.

Every fund I have real money in (a lot or a SIP outside paper buckets), or one bucket
has, with units and cost of what is still held.

One fund's lots (oldest first), with what was sold from each, and its SIPs, paper
ones too.

post.description:
Download the lists and update instruments, as ``friday instruments refresh`` does.
Each list is its own transaction; a failed one is reported, not raised.

get.description: Find instruments by part of a name, a symbol, an AMFI scheme code or an ISIN.
When each instrument list was last refreshed.

delete.description: Go back to the rule-based classification.

put.description: Set my own allocation split and exposure. It wins over the rules and survives refresh.

get.description: Whether a fund is tracked, which NAV dates Friday has, and its headline figures.
A fund's NAVs, oldest first.

delete.description: Stop keeping this fund's NAVs up to date. NAVs already stored stay.

put.description: Keep this fund's NAVs. Sync it afterwards to download its history.

post.description: Record a lump sum. The fund becomes tracked for NAVs.

delete.description: Delete a lump sum that nothing was sold from.

put.description:
Change a lot's figures, or skip a SIP instalment. Edited and skipped instalments are
kept when the SIP is rebuilt.

post.description: Weights must add up to exactly 100. Every fund and the benchmark become tracked.

get.description: The Nifty 50 index fund new models are compared with, if the fund list has it.

delete.description: Delete a model and its saved backtests. Its funds' NAVs stay.

get.description: Saved runs of a model, newest first.

post.description: A copy named "<name> copy": same funds, weights, benchmark and rebalance; no backtests.

get.description: Every tracked fund with the NAV dates Friday has, and the last sync.

post.description: Download missing NAVs for every tracked fund, or only the given ones.

Where new cash should go in a bucket: emergency top-up first (real buckets), then the
funds of its model furthest below their weights, never selling. Large amounts in a real
bucket come with a monthly stagger plan. Nothing is saved.

Buy a paper bucket's plan for the amount: one purchase per fund that gets money, at
its latest NAV.

get.description: Emergency goal and fund, the minimum per fund and the staggering rule.
Real money (purchases in no bucket or a real one), or one bucket's.

Value, invested and the benchmark over time, from ``start`` (or the first purchase)
to the latest NAV date, with the gain and return over that range. Real money, or one
bucket.

post.description: Take units out of the lots picked, all of one fund, on one date.

delete.description: Undo a sale from one lot: its units go back into the lot.

post.description:
Start a SIP. Instalments are added for every month the stored NAVs cover, and after
each NAV sync.

delete.description: Delete a SIP and its instalments, if nothing was sold from them.

put.description: Change a SIP and rebuild its instalments, keeping edited, skipped and sold ones.
